purpose: Dupilumab is used to treat conditions where your immune system overreacts and causes inflammation, such as moderate-to-severe eczema (atopic dermatitis), asthma, chronic sinusitis with nasal polyps, eosinophilic esophagitis, and prurigo nodularis. It helps reduce symptoms like itching, rashes, and breathing difficulties. Your doctor may prescribe it when other treatments have not worked well enough.
how_it_works: Your immune system produces certain proteins called IL-4 and IL-13 that can cause inflammation and trigger allergic reactions in your skin, lungs, and other areas. Dupilumab works by blocking these proteins so they cannot send the signal that causes inflammation. Think of it like putting a lock on a door so the troublemaking signals cannot get through — this helps calm down the overactive immune response.
common_side_effects: Injection site reactions such as redness, swelling, or pain where you give the shot. Eye problems like redness, itchiness, or watering eyes (conjunctivitis) are fairly common, especially in eczema patients. Some people also experience cold sore flare-ups (oral herpes) or joint pain.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have any eye problems, as dupilumab can sometimes worsen or cause eye inflammation. Do not stop any other medications, especially oral steroids, without talking to your doctor first. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you have a parasitic (helminth) infection, tell your doctor before starting this medication. This is an injection given under the skin, so never inject into skin that is damaged, bruised, or tender.
typical_dosing: Dupilumab is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection) every 2 to 4 weeks, depending on your condition and age. For most adults with eczema, a starting dose is given first, followed by a maintenance dose every 2 weeks. Your doctor or nurse will show you how to inject it at home using a pre-filled syringe or auto-injector pen. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
